en.statement: Digital transformation is Google's term for routine replacement of aging IT hardware.
en.explanation: Google defines digital transformation around changing business processes, culture, and customer experiences through digital technologies. A routine hardware refresh is a narrower activity.

en.statement: Public cloud customers draw computing capacity from a provider's shared resource pool.
en.explanation: Public cloud providers make pooled capacity available on demand. Customers consume allocated resources rather than needing a dedicated physical estate for each deployment.

en.statement: Google Cloud uses open standards to support integration with other vendors' technologies.
en.explanation: Google Cloud describes its open platform as a way to preserve technology choice and let partners integrate their offerings.

en.statement: Selecting tools to carry out a multistep task is a capability of agentic AI systems.
en.explanation: An agentic system can turn a goal into actions and use tools to carry them out. This extends its role beyond producing a response for a person to act on.

en.statement: AI Hypercomputer is Google's processor architecture for training AI models.
en.explanation: AI Hypercomputer is an integrated system that combines AI-optimized hardware, software, and consumption options. The name refers to the wider system rather than a processor architecture.

en.statement: Increasing the memory assigned to an existing virtual machine is vertical scaling.
en.explanation: Vertical scaling changes the resources of an existing instance. Adding memory is one way to increase that instance's capacity.

en.statement: Cloud elasticity means keeping peak-demand capacity allocated during quiet periods.
en.explanation: Elasticity adjusts allocated capacity as demand changes. When demand falls, resources can shrink instead of remaining sized for the peak.

en.statement: Cloud agility describes an application's uninterrupted operation during hardware failures.
en.explanation: Cloud agility concerns quickly trying, developing, and deploying changes. On-demand access to development tools and platforms shortens the path from an idea to a working application.

en.statement: Premium Tier hands global network traffic to the public internet near its source region.
en.explanation: Premium Tier outbound traffic typically rides Google's global network to a point of presence as close as possible to the internet user. Handing traffic off at a PoP near the region is Standard Tier behavior.

en.statement: A private cloud is defined by its physical location inside the customer's own building.
en.explanation: A private cloud is dedicated to one organization. It can be hosted on the organization's premises or at an off-site provider facility.

en.statement: Integrating an on-premises environment with a public cloud creates a hybrid cloud.
en.explanation: Applications then run on a mix of compute, storage and services across environments. Many migrations end up hybrid because workloads move to the cloud gradually.

en.statement: A deployment can become multicloud by spreading across multiple Google Cloud regions.
en.explanation: Multicloud involves services from different cloud providers. Deploying across regions of the same provider is still a single-provider deployment.

en.statement: DNS translates a website's domain name into the IP address used to reach it.
en.explanation: DNS records associate names with information such as IP addresses, allowing applications to find destinations by name.

en.statement: Network bandwidth describes the time a packet takes to reach its destination.
en.explanation: Bandwidth expresses data-transfer capacity per unit of time, commonly in bits per second. It describes a rate rather than a packet's travel duration.

en.statement: A Google Cloud zone is a deployment area within a particular geographic region.
en.explanation: Google Cloud organizes deployment locations into regions and zones. A zone belongs to a region rather than spanning several regions.

en.statement: A Cloud CDN edge cache is the authoritative copy of a website's content.
en.explanation: A Cloud CDN cache holds copies of content obtained from an origin. When suitable content is missing from the cache, Cloud CDN retrieves it from that origin.

en.statement: In IaaS, the customer administers the guest operating system running in a virtual machine.
en.explanation: IaaS leaves the guest operating system under customer management. The customer chooses and maintains the operating system used by its workload.

source.title: PaaS vs. IaaS vs. SaaS: What's the difference?

en.statement: PaaS lets developers deploy their own application code on a provider-managed platform.
en.explanation: PaaS supplies an application development and deployment environment. Teams build custom applications using that managed environment.

source.title: PaaS vs. IaaS vs. SaaS: What's the difference?

en.statement: In SaaS, customers patch the application software hosted by the service provider.
en.explanation: The SaaS provider maintains and updates the hosted application software. Customers use the application as a service rather than patching its hosted code.

source.title: PaaS vs. IaaS vs. SaaS: What's the difference?

en.statement: Email addresses customers give directly to a retailer are first-party data for that retailer.
en.explanation: First-party data comes from an organization's direct interactions with its customers. The relationship through which the data is collected determines this classification.

en.statement: Rows in a relational table follow predefined column names and data types.
en.explanation: A predefined schema organizes structured data into named fields with specified types. Relational tables are a common example of this organization.

en.statement: JSON records with named fields are classified as unstructured data.
en.explanation: JSON is semi-structured data: keys and nesting provide organization while allowing records to vary in their fields.

source.title: Working with JSON data in GoogleSQL

en.statement: A data warehouse supports analysis of historical information combined from multiple sources.
en.explanation: A warehouse brings data together to support reporting and analysis over time. This consolidated history helps analysts examine trends across business systems.

en.statement: A data lake converts incoming records to a fixed tabular schema before storing them.
en.explanation: A data lake can retain raw data in its native format. A predefined tabular schema is not a prerequisite for ingesting that data.

en.statement: Recording a customer's purchase as it happens is a transactional database workload.
en.explanation: Transactional databases support operational activities such as recording orders and updating inventory. This workload centers on individual business events.

en.statement: Data governance can assign a data steward accountability for the proper use of data.
en.explanation: A data steward is a designated person with responsibility for particular data and its proper use. Stewardship makes governance responsibilities explicit.

en.statement: In an ELT pipeline, data transformation happens before data enters the destination system.
en.explanation: ELT loads extracted data into the destination first and then transforms it there. The destination's processing capabilities perform the transformation.

en.statement: Data lineage describes which users have permission to read a particular dataset.
en.explanation: Data lineage traces where data originates, how it moves, and how it is transformed. It records the data's journey rather than a list of permitted readers.

en.statement: A data silo is a repository designed for shared access across business departments.
en.explanation: A data silo holds information in an isolated system or team, making it difficult to combine or use across the organization.

en.statement: Cloud Storage organizes uploaded objects inside containers called buckets.
en.explanation: A bucket groups objects such as uploaded images or backup files. Each stored object belongs to a bucket.

en.statement: Spanner provides strongly consistent transactions across geographically distributed data.
en.explanation: Spanner provides transaction consistency across distributed deployments, supporting applications that need a dependable shared view of changing business data.

en.statement: Cloud SQL provides managed Oracle Database instances for transactional applications.
en.explanation: Cloud SQL supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. Oracle Database is not one of its supported database engines.

source.title: Cloud SQL for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server

en.statement: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL uses a columnar engine to accelerate eligible analytical queries.
en.explanation: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL can use column-oriented processing for analytical scans and aggregations alongside its row-oriented engine.

en.statement: Bigtable suits high-throughput workloads that store time-series sensor measurements.
en.explanation: Bigtable supports large volumes of time-series data, including IoT readings. Its design fits frequent keyed reads and writes over these records.

en.statement: BigQuery users provision database servers before running their analytical queries.
en.explanation: BigQuery provides a serverless analytical service. Google manages the underlying infrastructure rather than requiring users to provision database servers.

en.statement: Firestore stores application records in relational tables connected by foreign keys.
en.explanation: Firestore stores data in documents organized into collections. Its native model is document-oriented rather than relational tables with foreign-key relationships.

en.statement: Reading an object in Cloud Storage's Archive class requires an offline restoration step.
en.explanation: Cloud Storage Archive objects remain available through online access. Reading them does not require an offline restoration process.

en.statement: Autoclass changes an object's storage class based on how that object is accessed.
en.explanation: Autoclass uses access patterns to move eligible objects between storage classes. This helps adapt storage placement when future access patterns are uncertain.

en.statement: Database Migration Service suspends source writes for the duration of a continuous migration.
en.explanation: During continuous migration, the source can remain operational and accept writes. Database Migration Service replicates ongoing changes before the final cutover.

en.statement: Looker can apply centrally defined business metrics across reports through its semantic layer.
en.explanation: Looker centralizes metric definitions in its data model. Reports can reuse the same business logic rather than independently defining each calculation.

en.statement: Business users write SQL statements to create a query in a Looker Explore.
en.explanation: A Looker Explore lets users build queries by selecting modeled dimensions and measures in a field picker, rather than writing SQL.

en.statement: Looker imports BigQuery tables into its own database before it can build dashboards from them.
en.explanation: Looker connects to BigQuery and queries data there. Copying the source tables into a Looker-owned database is not a prerequisite for building dashboards.

en.statement: Looker supports placing interactive analytics inside an organization's own application.
en.explanation: Looker's embedding capabilities let an application present analytics within its existing user experience, instead of sending users to a separate BI interface.

en.statement: Pub/Sub lets a producer publish events independently of when consumers process them.
en.explanation: Pub/Sub provides asynchronous messaging. Producers hand messages to the service, separating message publication from consumer processing.

en.statement: Dataflow runs batch and streaming data pipelines using the same programming model.
en.explanation: Dataflow uses the Apache Beam programming model across both processing modes. Teams can use a common approach to define their data-processing logic.

en.statement: Managed Service for Apache Spark offers a serverless option for data-processing workloads.
en.explanation: Managed Service for Apache Spark can execute workloads through a serverless option, letting teams submit work rather than operate their own Spark clusters.

en.statement: Machine learning learns decision patterns from examples instead of hand-written rules.
en.explanation: Machine learning finds patterns in training examples. Those patterns help a model make predictions about new inputs.

en.statement: Generative AI answers requests by retrieving completed responses stored in its training data.
en.explanation: Generative AI creates content from learned patterns. Its defining task is content generation rather than looking up a stored, completed answer.

en.statement: A retailer can use predictive machine learning to estimate future demand from historical sales.
en.explanation: Demand forecasting uses historical patterns to estimate future sales. Retailers can use those estimates when planning inventory.

en.statement: Artificial intelligence is a specialized branch within the broader field of machine learning.
en.explanation: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence. AI also encompasses approaches that do not learn from training examples.

en.statement: Checking that required customer details are present tests the completeness dimension of data quality.
en.explanation: Completeness measures whether required information is present. A missing required customer field is a completeness issue.

en.statement: Checking that customer email addresses match a required format measures the accuracy dimension of data quality.
en.explanation: Format checks assess validity. Accuracy instead concerns whether a value correctly represents the real-world fact it describes.

en.statement: The uniqueness dimension measures whether a customer address agrees across separate business systems.
en.explanation: Uniqueness concerns duplicate data. Agreement between values representing the same information across systems is consistency.

en.statement: A model's high overall accuracy establishes that it treats different customer groups fairly.
en.explanation: Overall accuracy measures prediction correctness rather than fairness across customer groups. Responsible AI evaluation also uses fairness measures that examine group outcomes.

en.statement: Machine learning can classify sentiment in free-text customer comments to reveal feedback patterns.
en.explanation: Sentiment analysis applies machine learning to written language. It can categorize the opinions expressed in customer feedback.

en.statement: Custom training gives an ML team less control over its model design than AutoML.
en.explanation: Custom training gives specialists control over their training approach and model design. AutoML prioritizes model development with less technical effort.

en.statement: Cloud Vision API extracts printed text from photos of product labels.
en.explanation: Cloud Vision API provides optical character recognition. A business can turn text visible in an image into machine-readable text.

source.title: Detect and extract text from images

en.statement: Cloud Translation glossaries help preserve a company's preferred translations of specialized terms.
en.explanation: A Cloud Translation glossary supplies domain-specific terminology, such as brand or product names, to keep translations consistent with business usage.

en.statement: Speech-to-Text labels the different speakers in a contact-center conversation transcript.
en.explanation: Speech-to-Text supports speaker diarization, which distinguishes speakers in an audio conversation. The resulting labels help readers follow who is speaking.

en.statement: Gemini interprets an image together with a written question about its contents.
en.explanation: Gemini supports multimodal input. A business application can combine visual material with text when requesting an analysis.

en.statement: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is a finished chat application for business end users.
en.explanation: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is a development platform for building and managing enterprise AI applications and agents, rather than a finished end-user chat application.

en.statement: Agent Studio can train new foundation models from scratch.
en.explanation: Agent Studio is a workspace for prototyping AI experiences with existing models and refining prompts. Training a foundation model from scratch is a different task.

en.statement: AutoML can train a business-specific prediction model using an organization's own examples.
en.explanation: AutoML uses a supplied dataset to develop a model for a particular prediction task. The training examples let that model reflect the organization's business problem.

source.title: Introduction to machine learning on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

en.statement: A Tensor Processing Unit can replace a virtual machine's CPU as a general-purpose processor.
en.explanation: A Tensor Processing Unit is a Google-designed accelerator specialized for machine learning workloads. It is not a general-purpose replacement for a CPU.

en.statement: Developing a model in BigQuery ML means writing Python code.
en.explanation: BigQuery ML creates and runs models from GoogleSQL queries or the Google Cloud console. Analysts build models with SQL skills they already have, without programming in Python or Java.

en.statement: Rehosting moves an existing application to the cloud with minimal changes to the application.
en.explanation: Rehosting is a migration strategy that preserves most of the existing application. It is commonly described as lift and shift.

source.title: Migration to Google Cloud: Get started

en.statement: Replatforming replaces an existing application with a newly built application designed from scratch.
en.explanation: Replatforming adapts and optimizes an existing workload for its new platform. Creating a replacement application from scratch is a different migration approach.

source.title: Migration to Google Cloud: Get started

en.statement: Migration discovery and assessment identifies which business applications depend on each other.
en.explanation: Dependency assessment reveals relationships that can affect a migration. It helps a team account for connected applications when planning which workloads to move.

source.title: Migration to Google Cloud: Assessing and discovering your workloads

en.statement: Migration assessment treats software licenses as transferable to cloud infrastructure by default.
en.explanation: Migration assessment includes checking software licensing restrictions. Some licenses prohibit cloud deployment or require a different licensing arrangement.

source.title: Migration to Google Cloud: Assessing and discovering your workloads

en.statement: In a migration inventory, a workload is the amount of traffic an application receives.
en.explanation: A migration inventory treats applications or services as workloads to assess and move. Incoming traffic is a characteristic of a workload rather than the workload itself.

source.title: Migration to Google Cloud: Assessing and discovering your workloads

en.statement: In serverless computing, the cloud provider operates the servers that execute application code.
en.explanation: Serverless computing shifts management of the underlying server infrastructure to the provider. The application still uses servers, but the team focuses on its code.

en.statement: A microservices architecture organizes its services into a single compulsory release unit.
en.explanation: A microservices architecture supports deploying services independently. A change to one service can be released separately from unrelated services.

en.statement: Containerization ties an application to the cloud provider where its container is created.
en.explanation: Containerization supports application portability across compatible environments. A container can move between development, data-center, and cloud environments.

en.statement: Spot VMs fit batch-processing jobs that can recover when their computing capacity is interrupted.
en.explanation: Spot VMs use capacity that Google Cloud can reclaim. Interruption-tolerant batch jobs can trade that availability risk for lower compute costs.

en.statement: Compute Engine suits an existing business application that needs a configurable virtual machine.
en.explanation: Compute Engine provides virtual machines for business workloads. It fits applications whose teams need control over the machine environment.

en.statement: Compute Engine is used for scientific workloads such as climate modeling and molecular simulations.
en.explanation: Compute Engine can provide high-performance computing resources for demanding simulations. Research workloads can use this capacity instead of relying entirely on local hardware.

en.statement: Google Kubernetes Engine is a proprietary replacement for the open-source Kubernetes platform.
en.explanation: Google Kubernetes Engine is a managed implementation of Kubernetes. It lets teams operate containerized applications using that open-source orchestration platform.

en.statement: A company using Snowflake needs to replace its warehouse with BigQuery before adopting Looker.
en.explanation: Looker supports connecting to Snowflake. A company can retain its Snowflake warehouse while using Looker for business intelligence.

en.statement: Cloud Run suits a custom web application whose team wants Google to manage its serving infrastructure.
en.explanation: Cloud Run is a managed application platform for workloads such as websites and web APIs. Google operates the infrastructure used to serve the application.

en.statement: Cloud Run suits interactive web requests rather than scheduled batch-processing workloads.
en.explanation: Cloud Run also supports jobs that perform batch work. Examples include recurring invoice generation and scheduled data processing.

en.statement: Generating a thumbnail when a customer uploads an image is a typical use for Cloud Run functions.
en.explanation: Cloud Run functions runs application code in response to events. Processing a newly uploaded file is a supported business use case.

en.statement: Adopting AlloyDB Omni requires rewriting PostgreSQL applications for a proprietary database interface.
en.explanation: AlloyDB Omni is PostgreSQL-compatible. Existing PostgreSQL applications can use it with their familiar database interface rather than requiring a proprietary rewrite.

en.statement: BigQuery Omni is an operational database service for recording customer orders across multiple clouds.
en.explanation: BigQuery Omni provides analytics over data in multiple cloud environments. Its role is analytical querying rather than serving as an application's transactional order database.

en.statement: Google Kubernetes Engine supports consistent application governance across cloud and on-premises environments.
en.explanation: GKE's cross-environment management capabilities help organizations apply consistent policies to their Kubernetes applications. This supports governance across a mixed estate.

en.statement: A web API lets one software application request functionality from another application.
en.explanation: An API exposes capabilities through an interface that other software can use. A partner application can integrate a service through that interface.

en.statement: Exposing a legacy service through Apigee requires a complete rewrite of its business logic.
en.explanation: Apigee can put an API layer in front of an existing service while leaving its backend unchanged. A full rewrite is not a prerequisite for exposing that service.

en.statement: In Apigee's terminology, an API consumer is the shopper using an application's checkout screen.
en.explanation: Apigee calls the app developer who builds with an API its consumer. The end customer using that developer's application is a different role.

en.statement: An API product in Apigee packages selected API capabilities with a service plan as a business offering.
en.explanation: Apigee API products package chosen functionality into offerings for particular audiences or service tiers. This gives a business a defined unit to offer as a product.

en.statement: An Apigee developer portal supports self-service onboarding for partners building client applications.
en.explanation: An Apigee developer portal lets developers learn about exposed services and register to use them. Partners can begin integrating through a self-service experience.

en.statement: Apigee API Analytics helps a business identify which API methods attract the most usage.
en.explanation: Apigee API Analytics reports API usage patterns. A business can use those observations to assess adoption and guide investment in its API program.

en.statement: Apigee's Advanced API Security analyzes API traffic to detect suspicious requests tied to API abuse.
en.explanation: It continuously monitors for threats such as malicious client attacks and API abuse, and offers tools for blocking or flagging the requests it finds.

en.statement: Customers can purchase paid API subscriptions in Apigee API hub, a public API marketplace.
en.explanation: Apigee API hub provides a central catalog for discovering and evaluating an organization's APIs. It is not a storefront for selling API subscriptions.

en.statement: Apigee's revenue-sharing feature pays API revenue shares to Google Cloud rather than developer partners.
en.explanation: Apigee monetization lets an API provider share revenue with developer partners. The feature supports that commercial partnership rather than paying a commission to Google Cloud.

en.statement: In Google's shared responsibility model, customers retain responsibility for their data access policies.
en.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, customers decide who can access their data. Moving that data to Google Cloud does not transfer those policy decisions to Google.

source.title: Shared responsibilities and shared fate on Google Cloud

en.statement: A DDoS attack aims to steal confidential records from an online service.
en.explanation: A distributed denial-of-service attack disrupts availability by overwhelming a service with traffic. Its defining objective is to prevent legitimate use rather than extract records.

en.statement: Ransomware infiltrates systems to hijack, encrypt, or steal data and then demand a ransom.
en.explanation: Ransomware uses control of a victim's data as leverage for extortion. As it spreads, it can encrypt data with keys from its command and control server and exfiltrate data.

source.title: Mitigate ransomware attacks using Google Cloud

en.statement: A fake payroll email asking an employee for credentials on a fraudulent website is a phishing attempt.
en.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to obtain sensitive information. Impersonating a familiar workplace service makes the request appear credible.

en.statement: Data integrity protects confidential information from being viewed by unauthorized readers.
en.explanation: Data integrity concerns the accuracy and trustworthiness of information. Confidentiality concerns keeping that information from unauthorized readers.

en.statement: Least privilege limits an employee's permissions to those needed for assigned work.
en.explanation: Least privilege grants access according to the tasks a person needs to perform. Broad administrative access is inappropriate when narrower permissions meet those needs.

en.statement: Zero-trust security trusts users on the corporate network because of their network location.
en.explanation: Zero-trust security requires verification regardless of network location. Being inside the corporate network does not establish that a user should be trusted.

en.statement: Encryption converts readable business data into ciphertext that requires a key to recover.
en.explanation: Encryption transforms plaintext into an unreadable form called ciphertext. Decryption uses a key to recover the original information.

en.statement: Authentication determines which actions a signed-in user is permitted to perform.
en.explanation: Authentication verifies an identity. Authorization determines which resources and actions that identity can access.

source.title: Authentication for Google Cloud APIs and services

en.statement: A username and password provide two different authentication factors during a cloud sign-in.
en.explanation: A username identifies an account; it is not a second authentication factor. Two-factor authentication requires additional proof beyond the password.

en.statement: Google Threat Intelligence draws its evidence from Google services rather than Mandiant investigations.
en.explanation: Google Threat Intelligence combines Google visibility, Mandiant investigative expertise, and VirusTotal intelligence. Mandiant findings are part of the offering rather than an excluded source.

en.statement: Security Command Center identifies cloud misconfigurations that expose business data.
en.explanation: Security Command Center reports security findings about cloud resources. These include configuration weaknesses that could put an organization's data at risk.

en.statement: Google Security Operations can scan application code for vulnerabilities before release.
en.explanation: Google Security Operations analyzes security telemetry to help teams detect and investigate threats. Its purpose is security operations rather than scanning application source code.

en.statement: Model Armor screens an AI assistant's prompts and responses for malicious instructions.
en.explanation: Model Armor evaluates prompts and model responses for threats such as prompt injection. This helps protect AI applications from attempts to manipulate their behavior.

en.statement: Google Cloud Armor is a service for defending an online shop against distributed denial-of-service attacks.
en.explanation: Google Cloud Armor provides protection for web applications against DDoS attacks. It can filter malicious traffic before that traffic reaches an application.

en.statement: Sensitive Data Protection can mask personal identifiers before a dataset is shared for analysis.
en.explanation: Sensitive Data Protection offers de-identification techniques, including masking sensitive values. A business can reduce exposure of personal information while retaining useful data.

en.statement: Identity-Aware Proxy can connect remote employees to a corporate network through a VPN tunnel.
en.explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy controls access to applications based on identity and access policy. It provides application-level access rather than acting as a VPN connection to the corporate network.

en.statement: Confidential Computing is designed to protect data traveling between a user's device and a server.
en.explanation: Confidential Computing protects data in use while it is being processed. Protecting data as it travels between endpoints addresses data in transit instead.

en.statement: Google Cloud's shared fate model extends security support to guidance and secure deployment blueprints.
en.explanation: In the shared fate model, Google works proactively with customers on their security journey. Recommended landing zones and security blueprints are examples of that support.

source.title: Shared responsibilities and shared fate on Google Cloud

en.statement: Data residency describes the legal authority governing data rather than its physical storage location.
en.explanation: Data residency concerns where data is physically stored or processed. Data sovereignty concerns the laws and regulations governing that data.

en.statement: Pay-as-you-go cloud usage is classified as capital expenditure because it provides long-term IT value.
en.explanation: Pay-as-you-go cloud services are operating expenditure. This consumption model shifts spending away from upfront investment in owned infrastructure.

source.title: A Guide to Financial Governance in the Cloud

en.statement: Cloud unit economics measures the total monthly cloud bill regardless of the business activity it supports.
en.explanation: Cloud unit economics relates spending to business activity, such as cost per customer served. It evaluates cost efficiency relative to that activity rather than total spending alone.

source.title: Maximize Business Value with Cloud FinOps

en.statement: In Cloud FinOps, finance manages cloud spending independently of engineering and business teams.
en.explanation: Cloud FinOps brings finance, technology, and business teams together to manage cloud value. Financial accountability is shared rather than isolated in the finance department.

source.title: Maximize Business Value with Cloud FinOps

en.statement: In Google Cloud's resource hierarchy, folders are a way to group projects by department or business unit.
en.explanation: Folders provide a grouping layer above projects. An organization can use them to reflect its departments, teams, or other organizational boundaries.

en.statement: The organization resource represents a company's top-level ownership of Google Cloud resources.
en.explanation: An organization resource is the root of the resource hierarchy. It places resource ownership with the organization rather than individual employees.

en.statement: Compute Engine committed use discounts are designed for predictable, steady VM usage.
en.explanation: Compute Engine offers discounted resource pricing in exchange for a usage commitment. Predictable, steady demand helps a business use the resources it commits to.

en.statement: Active Assist can negotiate custom service prices with Google to lower a customer's monthly cloud bill.
en.explanation: Active Assist recommends ways to optimize resource use, such as removing idle resources or reducing overprovisioning. It is an optimization adviser rather than a service-price negotiator.

source.title: Understanding how cost savings are calculated in recommendations

en.statement: A saved Google Cloud Pricing Calculator estimate is a binding price quote for a planned deployment.
en.explanation: The Google Cloud Pricing Calculator estimates costs from a proposed configuration. An estimate supports planning rather than guaranteeing the charges for actual consumption.

en.statement: Cloud Billing reports show which Google Cloud services contribute most to an organization's costs.
en.explanation: Cloud Billing reports break down incurred costs by dimensions such as service. This helps a team identify the services driving its cloud spending.

source.title: Analyze billing data and cost trends with Reports

en.statement: Dynamic Workload Scheduler suits AI training jobs that can wait for GPU resources to become available.
en.explanation: Dynamic Workload Scheduler can schedule training around resource availability. Jobs with flexible start times can use this approach instead of requiring immediate capacity.

source.title: Schedule training jobs based on resource availability

en.statement: Cloud Monitoring can alert an operations team when a service's latency exceeds an agreed threshold.
en.explanation: Cloud Monitoring evaluates collected metrics against alerting conditions. A performance threshold can trigger a notification to the team responsible for the service.

en.statement: Cloud Logging helps investigate an outage by searching event records from affected applications.
en.explanation: Cloud Logging provides searchable application and service logs. During an incident, these records help a team reconstruct what happened.

en.statement: Cloud Trace helps network teams benchmark the data-transfer capacity of connections between company offices.
en.explanation: Cloud Trace examines latency in application requests, including requests that cross multiple services. It helps locate delays within an application rather than benchmark office network capacity.

en.statement: Cloud Profiler shows developers which application code consumes excessive CPU or memory resources.
en.explanation: Cloud Profiler attributes CPU and memory use to application code. Developers can use that information to focus optimization work on resource-intensive parts of the application.

en.statement: Error Reporting is Google Cloud's public dashboard for tracking regional infrastructure outages.
en.explanation: Error Reporting helps teams identify and prioritize errors in their applications. It is an application troubleshooting tool rather than a public cloud service-status dashboard.

en.statement: A live replica lets a business restore records to their state before an application error corrupted them.
en.explanation: A replica is a continuously updated copy, so records corrupted by an application or operator error reach it too. Replication protects against infrastructure failure; a backup keeps an earlier known good state.

source.title: Data protection options for disks and instances

en.statement: The observed proportion of successful requests to a service is a common service level indicator.
en.explanation: A service level indicator is a measured aspect of service performance. The fraction of requests served successfully is one way to measure availability.

en.statement: A service level objective is a customer contract specifying compensation for missed reliability targets.
en.explanation: A service level objective defines a measurable performance target. A service level agreement is the agreement that can specify consequences for failing to meet service commitments.

en.statement: DevOps encourages development and operations teams to share responsibility for software delivery.
en.explanation: DevOps is a cultural and organizational approach that promotes shared ownership across software stakeholders. Delivery is a joint concern rather than a handoff between isolated teams.

en.statement: The saturation golden signal tracks how many requests a web service receives per minute.
en.explanation: Saturation measures how close a service is to exhausting its constrained resources. Request volume per unit of time is a traffic measure instead.
